name: Stack
description: Layout. direction "column" (default) or "row"; rows wrap. gap "none"|"s"|"m"|"l", default "m".
signature: Stack(children: any[], direction?: "column" | "row", gap?: "none" | "s" | "m" | "l")

examples.name: Column
examples.code: root = Stack([Text("First"), Text("Second")])

examples.name: Row
examples.code: root = Stack([Text("Left"), Text("Right")], "row", "l")

name: Card
description: A framed group of parts with an optional title. variant "card" (default) has a hairline frame; "sunk" is a muted tile, good for options side by side; "clear" has no frame. A "card" inside another Card draws as "sunk". Cards in a Row or Grid share one height.
signature: Card(children: any[], title?: string, variant?: "card" | "sunk" | "clear")

examples.name: Card
examples.code: root = Card([Text("Two blockers remain before the release."), Stack([Badge("In review", "info"), Badge("Due Fri")], "row", "s")], "Release 2.4")

examples.name: Nested
examples.code: root = Card([Row([Card([Text("Ship Friday with the known bug.")], "Ship"), Card([Text("Wait a week for the fix.")], "Wait")])], "Two options")

examples.name: Variants
examples.code: root = Stack([Card([Text("A hairline frame.")], "Card"), Card([Text("A muted tile.")], "Sunk", "sunk"), Card([Text("No frame, only spacing.")], "Clear", "clear")])

name: Row
description: Parts side by side in equal columns. Each column is at least 10rem wide, so a narrow screen wraps them. gap "none"|"s"|"m"|"l", default "l". For buttons or small items at their own width, use Stack with "row".
signature: Row(children: any[], gap?: "none" | "s" | "m" | "l")

examples.name: Three columns
examples.code: root = Row([Card([Text("Postgres")], "Database", "sunk"), Card([Text("Redis")], "Cache", "sunk"), Card([Text("S3")], "Files", "sunk")])

name: Grid
description: Tiles on an even grid. With no columns it fits as many tiles of about 10rem as there is room for. columns (1 to 6) asks for that many; a narrow screen shows fewer, each at least 8rem. Tiles in a row share one height.
signature: Grid(children: any[], columns?: number)

examples.name: Fit to width
examples.code: root = Grid([Stat("Users", 1240), Stat("Teams", 86), Stat("Seats", 3100), Stat("Churn", "2.1%"), Stat("NPS", 48)])

examples.name: Two columns
examples.code: root = Grid([Card([Text("Faster builds.")], "Pro", "sunk"), Card([Text("A smaller bundle.")], "Pro", "sunk"), Card([Text("A new config format.")], "Con", "sunk"), Card([Text("One more plugin to keep.")], "Con", "sunk")], 2)

name: Carousel
description: A row of slides that scrolls sideways, with previous and next buttons. Each item is one slide, often a Card or an Entity. Slides are about 16rem wide. label names the carousel for screen readers.
signature: Carousel(items: any[], label?: string)

examples.name: Cards
examples.code: root = Carousel([Card([Text("Kyoto, 3 nights")], "Day 1-3", "sunk"), Card([Text("Nara, day trip")], "Day 4", "sunk"), Card([Text("Osaka, 2 nights")], "Day 5-6", "sunk"), Card([Text("Fly home")], "Day 7", "sunk")], "Trip plan")

name: Details
description: A collapsible section: the title shows, the content opens on click. Closed unless open is true. Use it for detail most readers skip.
signature: Details(title: string, children: any[], open?: boolean)

examples.name: Closed and open
examples.code: root = Stack([Details("Why this works", [Text("The cache holds the last good build, so a retry is cheap.")]), Details("Steps", [List(["Clear the cache", "Run the build", "Check the logs"], true)], true)])

name: Divider
description: A thin line between parts. With a label, the label sits in the middle of the line.
signature: Divider(label?: string)

examples.name: Plain and labelled
examples.code: root = Stack([Text("Above the line."), Divider(), Text("Below the line."), Divider("or"), Text("Another way.")])

name: Accordion
description: Stacked sections where one opens at a time; the first starts open. Clicking an open title closes it. Up and down arrows move between titles. While the reply streams, the newest section opens until the reader clicks one.
signature: Accordion(items: AccordionItem[])

examples.name: FAQ
examples.code: root = Accordion([AccordionItem("What is included?", [Text("Hosting, backups, and email support.")]), AccordionItem("Can I cancel?", [Text("Yes, any time. You keep access to the end of the month.")]), AccordionItem("Is there a free tier?", [Text("Yes, for one project.")])])

name: AccordionItem
description: One section of an Accordion: a title and its content.
signature: AccordionItem(title: string, children: any[])

name: Modal
description: A button that opens a dialog with the children inside. label is the button text; title heads the dialog and defaults to label. Escape, the close button, or a click outside closes it. Use it for detail or a Form that should not take room in the reply.
signature: Modal(label: string, children: any[], title?: string)

examples.name: Details in a dialog
examples.code: root = Modal("See the full log", [Text("The build failed at step 4 of 6."), Code("text", "error: cannot find module 'zod'")], "Build log")

examples.name: Form in a dialog
examples.code: root = Modal("Change the plan", [Form("plan", [Choice("tier", ["Free", "Pro", "Team"], "Tier")], [Button("Save")])])

name: Tabs
description: Switch between a few views of related content. The first tab shows first.
signature: Tabs(tabs: Tab[])

examples.name: Two tabs
examples.code: root = Tabs([Tab("Summary", [Text("Shipped on time.")]), Tab("Notes", [Text("Docs follow next week.", "muted")])])

name: Tab
description: One tab of Tabs: a label and its content.
signature: Tab(label: string, children: any[])

name: Heading
description: A section title inside the UI. The reply already names the UI, so do not open with one.
signature: Heading(text: string)

examples.name: Heading
examples.code: root = Stack([Heading("Open questions"), Text("Two remain.")])

name: Text
description: A paragraph of plain text. tone "default"|"muted"|"strong".
signature: Text(text: string, tone?: "default" | "muted" | "strong")

examples.name: Tones
examples.code: root = Stack([Text("Default text."), Text("Muted text.", "muted"), Text("Strong text.", "strong")])

name: Callout
description: A short highlighted note with a coloured side bar.
signature: Callout(tone: "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", title: string, body?: string)

examples.name: Tones
examples.code: root = Stack([Callout("info", "Heads up", "The API changes on Monday."), Callout("success", "Deployed"), Callout("warning", "Two blockers", "Fix them before Friday."), Callout("danger", "Build failed")])

name: Stat
description: One headline number. change is a short note under it, like "+12%" or "since May". trend "up" is good (green), "down" is bad (red), "neutral" (default) is muted. tone colours the value itself: "success", "warning", "danger", "info", or "neutral" (default, plain).
signature: Stat(label: string, value: string | number, change?: string, trend?: "neutral" | "up" | "down", tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", source?: string)

examples.name: With change
examples.code: root = Stat("Signups", 1240, "+12%", "up")

examples.name: Coloured value
examples.code: root = Stats([Stat("Failing tests", 3, "since main", "neutral", "danger"), Stat("Uptime", "99.98%", "30 days", "neutral", "success")])

name: Stats
description: A row of Stat numbers that wraps on narrow screens.
signature: Stats(items: Stat[])

examples.name: Three numbers
examples.code: root = Stats([Stat("Signups", 1240, "+12%", "up"), Stat("Churn", "2.1%", "+0.4%", "down"), Stat("Due", "Fri")])

name: Badge
description: A short status in a tinted pill, like "Shipped", "Blocked", or "3 open". tone "neutral" (default), "info", "success", "warning", or "danger". For a topic or category, use Tag.
signature: Badge(text: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

examples.name: Tones
examples.code: root = Stack([Badge("Draft"), Badge("In review", "info"), Badge("Shipped", "success"), Badge("At risk", "warning"), Badge("Blocked", "danger")], "row", "s")

name: Tag
description: A label for a topic, category, or owner, in a hairline outline. icon is an Icon name shown before the text. tone "neutral" (default), "info", "success", "warning", or "danger" colours the icon, or a small dot when there is no icon. For a status, use Badge.
signature: Tag(text: string, icon?: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

examples.name: Plain, dot, and icon
examples.code: root = Stack([Tag("design"), Tag("backend", null, "info"), Tag("Ana", "User"), Tag("Berlin", "MapPin", "danger")], "row", "s")

name: Chips
description: A wrapping row of tags. Each item is a plain string or a Tag. For chips the reader picks from, use Choice.
signature: Chips(items: (string | Tag)[])

examples.name: Strings and tags
examples.code: root = Chips(["react", "zod", "vitest", Tag("needs review", "Warning", "warning")])

name: Icon
description: A small icon at the size of the text around it. With no tone it takes the text colour; tone "neutral", "info", "success", "warning", or "danger" colours it. label is read by screen readers; leave it out when the icon only decorates. An unknown name shows nothing. Names: ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, Bell, Book, Bookmark, Briefcase, Bug, Building, Calendar, Car, ChartBar, ChartLine, Check, CircleCheck, CircleX, Clock, Cloud, Code, Coffee, CreditCard, Database, DollarSign, Download, ExternalLink, Eye, File, FileText, Flag, Folder, GitBranch, GitCommit, GitPullRequest, Globe, GraduationCap, Heart, Home, Image, Info, Key, Lightbulb, Link, Lock, Mail, MapPin, Message, Minus, Moon, Package, Pencil, Phone, Plane, Plus, Rocket, Search, Server, Settings, Shield, ShoppingCart, Sparkles, Star, Sun, Tag, Target, Terminal, Train, Trash, TrendingDown, TrendingUp, Upload, User, Users, Utensils, Warning, Wrench, X, Zap.
signature: Icon(name: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", label?: string)

examples.name: Inline and toned
examples.code: root = Stack([Icon("Check", "success", "Done"), Icon("Warning", "warning", "Warning"), Icon("CircleX", "danger", "Failed"), Icon("Rocket"), Icon("GitPullRequest", "info")], "row", "m")

name: Entity
description: One person, place, or thing: a picture, the name, a subtitle, and a few facts. facts is an object like {"Rating": 4.6, "Price": "$$"} or a list of [label, value] pairs. image is an http(s) or data: image URL; with none, a kind icon or the first letter stands in. url (http or https) makes the name a link. kind "person", "place", "org", "product", "link", or "other" (default). In a narrow tile, like a Grid or Carousel, the picture goes on top.
signature: Entity(name: string, subtitle?: string, image?: string, facts?: Record<string, any> | any[][], url?: string, kind?: "person" | "place" | "org" | "product" | "link" | "other")

examples.name: Place with photo
examples.code: root = Entity("Eiffel Tower", "Landmark in Paris", "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg/640px-Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg", {"Height": "330 m", "Opened": 1889, "Visitors": "6M a year"}, "https://www.toureiffel.paris", "place")

examples.name: Person, no photo
examples.code: root = Entity("Ana Lima", "Staff engineer, Payments", null, [["Team", "Payments"], ["Time zone", "UTC-3"]], null, "person")

examples.name: Tiles
examples.code: root = Grid([Entity("Kyoto", "3 nights", "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg/640px-Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg", {"From": "$180"}), Entity("Nara", "Day trip", null, {"Train": "45 min"}, null, "place"), Entity("Osaka", "2 nights", null, {"From": "$140"})])

name: File
description: A file reference in mono, as path or path:line. An http(s) URL opens on click; a workspace path shows as text.
signature: File(path: string, line?: number)

examples.name: Path and URL
examples.code: root = Stack([File("src/server/auth.ts", 42), File("README.md"), File("https://github.com/hemaaanth/oh-my-bb/blob/main/README.md")])

name: Image
description: A picture from an http(s) or data: image URL. alt describes it for screen readers, and shows in its place if it fails to load. caption is a line under it. Clicking it opens it full size. Other sources, like file paths, show the alt text.
signature: Image(src: string, alt: string, caption?: string)

examples.name: With caption
examples.code: root = Image("https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg/640px-Tour_Eiffel_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg", "The Eiffel Tower on a clear day", "Paris, from the Champ de Mars")

examples.name: Cannot load
examples.code: root = Image("/tmp/chart.png", "Weekly signups chart")

name: KeyValue
description: Labels and their values in two aligned columns; on a narrow screen each label sits above its value. pairs is an object like {"Owner": "Ana", "Due": "Fri"} or a list of [label, value] pairs. A value may be text, a number, null (shown as a dash), or a component such as Badge or File.
signature: KeyValue(pairs: Record<string, any> | any[][])

examples.name: Object
examples.code: root = KeyValue({"Owner": "Ana Lima", "Status": Badge("In review", "info"), "Due": "Fri 24 Oct", "Budget": 12000, "Notes": null})

examples.name: Pairs
examples.code: root = KeyValue([["Entry point", File("server.ts", 12)], ["Runtime", "Node 22"]])

name: List
description: A bulleted list, or a numbered one with ordered true. Each item is a string or a component, like File or Text. A List right after an item nests under it.
signature: List(items: any[], ordered?: boolean)

examples.name: Bullets
examples.code: root = List(["Faster builds", "Smaller bundle", "One config file"])

examples.name: Numbered, nested
examples.code: root = List(["Set up", List(["Install Node 22", "Run npm ci"]), "Build", File("dist/index.js"), "Deploy"], true)

name: Sources
description: The links an answer drew on, numbered in order, so "[2]" in the reply is the second. Each link is a URL string or a Source with a title and note. Only http(s) links open; another link keeps its number and says it cannot open. title heads the list, default "Sources".
signature: Sources(links: (string | Source)[], title?: string)

examples.name: With titles
examples.code: root = Sources([Source("https://react.dev/reference/react/useId", "useId", "Stable ids for accessibility attributes."), Source("https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/dialog", "The dialog element"), "https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/"])

name: Source
description: One cited link of Sources: an http(s) url, a title (the domain shows when it is missing), and an optional short note.
signature: Source(url: string, title?: string, note?: string)

name: Table
description: A data table. Each row is a list of cells in column order. Numbers align right. source is an optional caption or HTTPS URL; otherwise loaded files are credited. An empty source hides the caption.
signature: Table(columns: string[], rows: (string | number | any)[][], source?: string)

examples.name: Mixed cells
examples.code: root = Table(["Task", "Owner", "Days"], [["Copy", "Ana", 2], ["QA", "Raj", 5], ["Launch", "Ana", null]])

name: Progress
description: A labelled progress bar. max defaults to 100.
signature: Progress(label: string, value: number, max?: number)

examples.name: Two bars
examples.code: root = Stack([Progress("Done", 3, 5), Progress("Budget used", 72)])

name: Code
description: A code block with BB's highlighting. language is a file extension like "ts", "py", "sh", "json".
signature: Code(code: string, language?: string)

examples.name: TypeScript
examples.code: root = Code("export function add(a: number, b: number) {\n  return a + b;\n}", "ts")

name: Diff
description: A unified diff of one file in BB's diff viewer. patch is unified diff text with @@ hunks. file is its path.
signature: Diff(patch: string, file: string)

examples.name: One hunk

name: Snippet
description: A short line of code or text with a Copy button, like a command to run, an ID, or a URL. For longer code with highlighting use Code.
signature: Snippet(text: string, label?: string)

examples.name: Command
examples.code: root = Snippet("npm install @openuidev/react-lang", "Install")

examples.name: ID
examples.code: root = Snippet("thr_8f2a91c4")

name: FileCode
description: Read source lines from a real file in the thread workspace, thread storage, or /tmp. from and to are one-based inclusive lines; default is the file, at most 400 lines. Shows original line numbers and offers Copy and Open file. Published pages use the source captured at publish time. Unlike Snippet, this reads a file rather than copying supplied text.
signature: FileCode(file: string, from?: number, to?: number)

examples.name: Real line numbers
examples.code: root = FileCode("src/math.ts", 2, 4)

name: Gauge
description: One value on a half-circle dial from 0 to max (default 100), like a score or a utilisation. tone colours the dial: "info" (default), "success", "warning", "danger", or "neutral".
signature: Gauge(label: string, value: number, max?: number, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

examples.name: Score
examples.code: root = Gauge("Lighthouse score", 92, 100, "success")

examples.name: Two dials
examples.code: root = Stack([Gauge("CPU", 71, 100, "warning"), Gauge("Disk GB", 120, 512)], "row")

name: SegmentedBar
description: One bar split into parts by value, with a legend of each part's value and share, like a budget or a disk. Parts without a tone take the chart colours in order.
signature: SegmentedBar(parts: {label: string, value: number, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"}[], label?: string)

examples.name: Budget
examples.code: root = SegmentedBar([{label: "Design", value: 12000}, {label: "Build", value: 30000}, {label: "Launch", value: 8000}], "Budget")

examples.name: Disk with tones
examples.code: root = SegmentedBar([{label: "Used", value: 380, tone: "warning"}, {label: "Free", value: 132, tone: "neutral"}])

name: Sparkline
description: A tiny line of recent values with no axes, to show a trend at a glance next to text or in a Table cell's place. tone "info" (default), "success", "warning", "danger", or "neutral".
signature: Sparkline(values: number[], tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

examples.name: Up
examples.code: root = Sparkline([12, 14, 13, 17, 16, 21, 24], "success")

examples.name: Down
examples.code: root = Sparkline([9, 7, 8, 4, 5, 2], "danger")

name: Steps
description: Numbered steps in order, joined by a line, like a setup guide or a plan. status "done", "current", "todo" (default), or "blocked".
signature: Steps(items: {title: string, detail?: string, status?: "done" | "current" | "todo" | "blocked"}[])

examples.name: Setup
examples.code: root = Steps([{title: "Create the project", status: "done"}, {title: "Connect GitHub", detail: "Pick the repositories BB may read.", status: "current"}, {title: "Invite the team"}])

examples.name: Blocked
examples.code: root = Steps([{title: "Build", status: "done"}, {title: "Deploy", detail: "Waiting on a production approval.", status: "blocked"}, {title: "Announce"}])

name: Timeline
description: Events in order along a line, like a changelog, an incident, or a history. time is free text such as "09:42" or "May 2026". tone colours the dot: "neutral" (default), "info", "success", "warning", or "danger".
signature: Timeline(items: {time?: string, title: string, detail?: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"}[])

examples.name: Incident
examples.code: root = Timeline([{time: "09:42", title: "Alert fired", detail: "p95 latency over 2 s.", tone: "danger"}, {time: "09:50", title: "Rolled back v2.14", tone: "warning"}, {time: "10:05", title: "Resolved", tone: "success"}])

examples.name: History
examples.code: root = Timeline([{time: "Jan 2026", title: "Beta"}, {time: "May 2026", title: "1.0"}, {time: "Oct 2026", title: "Teams", detail: "Shared projects and roles."}])

name: Tree
description: A collapsible tree. Each item is a path string ("src/app/main.ts"; paths that share folders merge) or {label, note?, children?}, where children is a list of the same kind of items. note is short muted text after the label. Folders start open while the tree stays short.
signature: Tree(items: (string | {label: string, note?: string, children?: any[]})[])

examples.name: File paths
examples.code: root = Tree(["src/app/main.ts", "src/app/routes.ts", "src/lib/db.ts", "package.json", "README.md"])

examples.name: Labels and notes
examples.code: root = Tree([{label: "Company", children: [{label: "Engineering", note: "24", children: [{label: "Platform", note: "9"}, {label: "Product", note: "15"}]}, {label: "Design", note: "6"}]}])

name: Calendar
description: A month calendar with events. date is "yyyy-mm-dd". month "yyyy-mm" picks the month shown first; it defaults to the first event's month, then today. People step between months and pick a day to see its events. tone colours an event: "info" (default), "success", "warning", "danger", or "neutral".
signature: Calendar(events: {date: string, title: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"}[], month?: string)

examples.name: Launch month
examples.code: root = Calendar([{date: "2026-11-03", title: "Design review"}, {date: "2026-11-12", title: "Code freeze", tone: "warning"}, {date: "2026-11-12", title: "QA starts"}, {date: "2026-11-19", title: "Launch", tone: "success"}], "2026-11")

name: CalendarHeatmap
description: Daily counts as a GitHub-style grid of weeks, from the first date to the last. date is "yyyy-mm-dd"; missing days count as 0 and repeated dates add up. label names what is counted, like "Commits". tone colours the cells: "success" (default), "info", "warning", "danger", or "neutral".
signature: CalendarHeatmap(days: {date: string, value: number}[], label?: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

name: Diagram
description: A flow diagram of boxes and arrows, laid out in layers. Each node has an id and an optional label (defaults to the id). Each edge goes from one node id to another, with an optional short label. direction "down" (default) or "right". tone outlines a node: "info", "success", "warning", "danger", or "neutral" (default). Keep it under about 15 nodes.
signature: Diagram(nodes: {id: string, label?: string, tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"}[], edges: {from: string, to: string, label?: string}[], direction?: "down" | "right")

examples.name: Flow
examples.code: root = Diagram([{id: "req", label: "Request"}, {id: "auth", label: "Auth"}, {id: "cache", label: "Cache"}, {id: "db", label: "Database"}, {id: "res", label: "Response", tone: "success"}], [{from: "req", to: "auth"}, {from: "auth", to: "cache"}, {from: "cache", to: "res", label: "hit"}, {from: "cache", to: "db", label: "miss"}, {from: "db", to: "res"}])

examples.name: Left to right with a loop
examples.code: root = Diagram([{id: "draft", label: "Draft"}, {id: "review", label: "Review", tone: "info"}, {id: "ship", label: "Ship", tone: "success"}], [{from: "draft", to: "review"}, {from: "review", to: "draft", label: "changes"}, {from: "review", to: "ship"}], "right")

name: Chart
description: A chart of Series. Ordinal types use one value per label. Histogram and box use raw observations: histogram labels are increasing numeric bin edges, or [] for shared automatic bins; box draws quartiles, 1.5 IQR whiskers and outliers. Heatmap uses labels as columns and Series as rows. scatter reads numeric labels as x values. source identifies where the numbers came from. xLabel and yLabel name the axes.
signature: Chart(type: "bar" | "line" | "area" | "stackedBar" | "horizontalBar" | "pie" | "donut" | "radar" | "radial" | "scatter" | "funnel" | "histogram" | "box" | "heatmap", labels: (string | number)[], series: Series[], title?: string, xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, source?: string)

examples.code: root = Chart("funnel", ["Visited", "Signed up", "Activated", "Paid"], [Series("Users", [5000, 1200, 640, 180])], "Signup funnel")

examples.name: Histogram
examples.code: root = Chart("histogram", [], [Series("Before", [11, 12, 12, 15, 16, 20, 31]), Series("After", [8, 9, 10, 11, 11, 13])], "Request latency", "Milliseconds", "Requests", "Illustrative")

examples.name: Box plot
examples.code: root = Chart("box", [], [Series("Before", [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 45]), Series("After", [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12])], "Latency distribution", "Milliseconds")

examples.name: Heatmap
examples.code: root = Chart("heatmap", ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"], [Series("API", [8, 2, 5]), Series("Worker", [1, 9, 4])], "Failures by day")

name: Series
description: One named series of a Chart. Ordinal charts take one value per label; histogram and box take raw observations and leave out non-numeric values. null leaves a gap. Optional tone: neutral, info, success, warning, danger.
signature: Series(name: string, values: (number | string | any)[], tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger")

name: Input
description: A one-line text field. Bind value to a $variable to use it elsewhere.
signature: Input(name: string, label?: string, placeholder?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: With label
examples.code: root = Input("title", "Title", "Name the release")

examples.name: Bound
examples.code:
$name = "Ada"
root = Stack([Input("name", "Name", null, $name), Text("Hello, " + $name, "muted")])

name: TextArea
description: A text field for a few lines or more. The reader can drag it taller.
signature: TextArea(name: string, label?: string, placeholder?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: Notes
examples.code: root = TextArea("notes", "Anything else?", "Context, constraints, links")

examples.name: Preset
examples.code: root = TextArea("summary", "Summary", null, "Ship the beta to 5% of users on Monday.\nRoll back if errors pass 1%.")

name: Slider
description: A number slider. Bind value to a $variable to drive other components live.
signature: Slider(name: string, min: number, max: number, step?: number, label?: string, value?: $binding<number>)

examples.name: Drives a Text
examples.code:
$budget = 40
root = Stack([Slider("budget", 0, 100, 5, "Budget", $budget), Text("Budget: " + $budget + "%", "muted")])

name: Stepper
description: A whole or decimal number with - and + buttons, for counts and small amounts. step defaults to 1; it starts at value, else min, else 0. Arrow keys step, Page Up/Down step by 10.
signature: Stepper(name: string, label?: string, min?: number, max?: number, step?: number, value?: $binding<number>)

examples.name: Count
examples.code: root = Stepper("seats", "Seats", 1, 20, 1, 3)

examples.name: Decimals, bound
examples.code:
$ratio = 1.5
root = Stack([Stepper("ratio", "Ratio", 0, 3, 0.25, $ratio), Text("Ratio " + $ratio, "muted")])

examples.name: No bounds
examples.code: root = Stepper("offset", "Offset")

name: DateInput
description: A date picker. value, min, and max are yyyy-mm-dd dates, and the answer is sent the same way.
signature: DateInput(name: string, label?: string, min?: string, max?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: Empty
examples.code: root = DateInput("due", "Due")

name: Rating
description: Stars from 1 to max (default 5, at most 10). 0 means not rated yet. Picking the current star again clears it.
signature: Rating(name: string, label?: string, max?: number, value?: $binding<number>)

examples.name: Rated
examples.code: root = Rating("quality", "How good was the answer?", 5, 4)

examples.name: Ten, unrated
examples.code: root = Rating("likely", "How likely are you to recommend us?", 10)

name: Toggle
description: An on/off switch.
signature: Toggle(name: string, label: string, value?: $binding<boolean>)

examples.name: Toggle
examples.code: root = Toggle("notify", "Notify me")

name: Choice
description: Pick one option, or several with multiple true. Shown as pills, so keep options short; options are strings or {label, value?, detail?}; value defaults to label and is what is sent. For options that need a line of detail use Radio or CheckBoxGroup; for a long list use Select.
signature: Choice(name: string, options: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string})[], label?: string, multiple?: boolean, value?: $binding<string | string[]>)

examples.name: One
examples.code: root = Choice("channel", ["Email", "Ads", "Social"], "Channel")

examples.name: Several
examples.code: root = Choice("days", ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"], "Days", true, ["Mon", "Wed"])

name: Radio
description: Pick exactly one option from a short column of radio buttons; options are strings or {label, value?, detail?}; value defaults to label and is what is sent, and detail shows under the option. Arrow keys move the pick.
signature: Radio(name: string, options: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string})[], label?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: With detail
examples.code: root = Radio("plan", [{label: "Starter", detail: "One project, community support"}, {label: "Team", detail: "Ten projects, email support"}, {label: "Business", value: "biz", detail: "Unlimited, SSO, a named contact"}], "Plan", "Team")

examples.name: Plain
examples.code: root = Radio("size", ["Small", "Medium", "Large"], "Size")

name: CheckBoxGroup
description: Tick any number of options in a column of checkboxes; options are strings or {label, value?, detail?}; value defaults to label and is what is sent. The ticked values are sent in option order.
signature: CheckBoxGroup(name: string, options: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string})[], label?: string, value?: $binding<string[]>)

examples.name: With detail
examples.code: root = CheckBoxGroup("checks", [{label: "Unit tests", detail: "vitest, about 40s"}, {label: "Type check"}, {label: "End-to-end", detail: "Playwright, about 6 min"}], "Run before merge", ["Unit tests", "Type check"])

name: Checklist
description: A to-do list the reader ticks off, with an "n of m done" count. items are strings or {label, value?, detail?}; value lists the items already done. Done items are sent.
signature: Checklist(name: string, items: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string})[], label?: string, value?: $binding<string[]>)

examples.name: Launch
examples.code: root = Checklist("launch", ["Freeze the branch", "Run the migration", {label: "Flip the flag", detail: "billing.v2 to 100%"}, "Post in #releases"], "Launch steps", ["Freeze the branch"])

examples.name: Empty
examples.code: root = Checklist("todo", [], "Nothing to do")

name: Select
description: Pick one option from a dropdown, good for long lists; options are strings or {label, value?, detail?}; value defaults to label and is what is sent. placeholder shows until a pick, default "Choose…".
signature: Select(name: string, options: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string})[], label?: string, placeholder?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: Region
examples.code: root = Select("region", ["us-east-1", "us-west-2", "eu-west-1", "eu-central-1", "ap-southeast-1", "ap-northeast-1"], "Region", "Pick a region")

examples.name: Labels and preset
examples.code: root = Select("tz", [{label: "London", value: "Europe/London"}, {label: "New York", value: "America/New_York"}, {label: "Tokyo", value: "Asia/Tokyo", detail: "UTC+9"}], "Time zone", null, "America/New_York")

name: OptionCards
description: Pick one of a few rich options shown as cards side by side, or several with multiple true. options are {label, value?, detail?, icon?, image?}; value defaults to label. image is a scoped file or https picture; its separate expand button does not change the choice. icon is one of: arrowdown, arrowleft, arrowright, arrowup, bell, bookmark, bug, calendar, check, chevrondown, chevronleft, chevronright, chevronup, help, clock, code, copy, download, more, external, eye, file, filter, folder, branch, heart, home, info, idea, link, lock, mail, minus, pause, edit, play, plus, refresh, rocket, search, send, settings, share, sparkles, star, thumbsdown, thumbsup, trash, warning, upload, user, close, zap.
signature: OptionCards(name: string, options: (string | {label: string, value?: string, detail?: string, icon?: string, image?: string})[], label?: string, multiple?: boolean, value?: $binding<string | string[]>)

examples.name: One
examples.code: root = OptionCards("approach", [{label: "Patch", icon: "zap", detail: "Fix the query in place. Fast, keeps the debt."}, {label: "Refactor", icon: "code", detail: "Move reads to the cache layer. Two days."}, {label: "Rewrite", icon: "rocket", detail: "New service. A sprint, cleanest result."}], "How should we fix it?", false, "Refactor")

examples.name: Several
examples.code: root = OptionCards("extras", [{label: "Dark mode"}, {label: "Export to CSV", detail: "From any table"}, {label: "Slack alerts", icon: "bell"}], "Add to the next release", true)

examples.name: Visual choices
examples.code: root = OptionCards("layout", [{"label":"List","image":"data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%22%20width%3D%22240%22%20height%3D%22120%22%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%22240%22%20height%3D%22120%22%20fill%3D%22%23f4f4f5%22%2F%3E%3Cpath%20d%3D%22M24%2028h192M24%2060h192M24%2092h192%22%20stroke%3D%22%232563eb%22%20stroke-width%3D%2216%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E"},{"label":"Columns","image":"data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%22%20width%3D%22240%22%20height%3D%22120%22%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%22240%22%20height%3D%22120%22%20fill%3D%22%23f4f4f5%22%2F%3E%3Cpath%20d%3D%22M52%2020v80M120%2020v80M188%2020v80%22%20stroke%3D%22%232563eb%22%20stroke-width%3D%2240%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E"}], "Choose a layout")

name: Swatches
description: Pick one colour from a row of chips. colors are CSS colours ("#2563eb", "oklch(0.7 0.1 200)") or {value, name?}; the chosen value is sent.
signature: Swatches(name: string, colors: (string | {value: string, name?: string})[], label?: string, value?: $binding<string>)

examples.name: Named
examples.code: root = Swatches("accent", [{value: "#2563eb", name: "Blue"}, {value: "#16a34a", name: "Green"}, {value: "#d97706", name: "Amber"}, {value: "#dc2626", name: "Red"}, {value: "#7c3aed", name: "Violet"}], "Accent colour", "#16a34a")

examples.name: Plain CSS
examples.code: root = Swatches("bg", ["white", "oklch(0.95 0.02 90)", "#0f172a"], "Background")

name: ListEditor
description: A list the reader grows, edits in place, and trims, such as names or tags. value is the starting list. Repeats are refused.
signature: ListEditor(name: string, label?: string, placeholder?: string, value?: $binding<string[]>)

examples.name: Tags
examples.code: root = ListEditor("tags", "Tags", "Add a tag", ["billing", "urgent"])

examples.name: Empty
examples.code: root = ListEditor("reviewers", "Reviewers", "Name or handle")

name: EditableTable
description: A small table the reader edits: change cells, add rows, remove rows. columns are keys or {key, label?, type?}; type "text", "number", or "boolean" (a checkbox), else the kind of the first filled cell. rows are the starting rows. The rows are sent as JSON.
signature: EditableTable(name: string, columns: (string | {key: string, label?: string, type?: "text" | "number" | "boolean"})[], label?: string, rows?: Record<string, any>[])

examples.name: Typed columns
examples.code: root = EditableTable("order", [{key: "item"}, {key: "qty", label: "Qty", type: "number"}, {key: "gift", label: "Gift wrap", type: "boolean"}], "Order", [{item: "Tea", qty: 2, gift: false}, {item: "Mug", qty: 1, gift: true}])

examples.name: Empty
examples.code: root = EditableTable("guests", ["name", "email"], "Guests")

name: Button
description: A button. With no action it sends its label (and its Form answers) to the assistant, then locks. variant "primary" (default) or "secondary".
signature: Button(label: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary")

examples.name: Variants
examples.code: root = Stack([Button("Ship it"), Button("Not yet", null, "secondary")], "row", "s")

name: IconButton
description: A square button that shows only an icon; label is its tooltip and screen reader name, and is what it sends, like Button. variant "secondary" (default, hairline frame), "primary" (solid), or "ghost" (no frame). icon is one of: arrowdown, arrowleft, arrowright, arrowup, bell, bookmark, bug, calendar, check, chevrondown, chevronleft, chevronright, chevronup, help, clock, code, copy, download, more, external, eye, file, filter, folder, branch, heart, home, info, idea, link, lock, mail, minus, pause, edit, play, plus, refresh, rocket, search, send, settings, share, sparkles, star, thumbsdown, thumbsup, trash, warning, upload, user, close, zap. An unknown icon shows the label instead.
signature: IconButton(label: string, icon: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost")

examples.name: Variants
examples.code: root = Stack([IconButton("Like", "thumbs-up", null, "primary"), IconButton("Retry", "refresh"), IconButton("More", "more", null, "ghost"), IconButton("Unknown icon", "kraken")], "row", "s")

name: FollowUps
description: Suggested next questions, at the end of a reply. Each prompt is a row the reader clicks to send its text to the thread as their next message. Keep 2 to 4 short prompts. label is a heading above them.
signature: FollowUps(prompts: string[], label?: string)

examples.name: Prompts
examples.code: root = FollowUps(["Show the slowest queries", "Compare with last week", "Draft the incident note"], "Next")

name: Form
description: Groups fields so a Button sends all their answers to the assistant in one message. A sent Form locks until the reader picks Edit answers.
signature: Form(name: string, fields: any[], buttons: (Button | IconButton)[])

examples.name: Form
examples.code: root = Form("launch", [Choice("channel", ["Email", "Ads"], "Channel"), Slider("budget", 0, 100, 5, "Budget"), Input("note", "Note")], [Button("Approve"), Button("Hold", null, "secondary")])

examples.name: Many fields
examples.code: root = Form("intake", [Radio("kind", ["Bug", "Feature", "Question"], "Kind"), DateInput("due", "Needed by"), Stepper("people", "People affected", 1, 1000), Rating("pain", "How painful?"), CheckBoxGroup("areas", ["API", "Web", "Mobile"], "Areas"), TextArea("details", "Details")], [Button("Send"), IconButton("Discard", "trash", null, "ghost")])

name: Map
description: Numbered Marker parts, place names, or trip records {name,lat?,lng?,note?,day?,wiki?}. Existing Area lists, center, zoom, panning, and popups work unchanged. As the second argument, {route:true,tour:true} joins stops by day and drops pins in sequence without moving the camera. Days inherit from the preceding stop. A Wikipedia lead photo is looked up only when its place opens and must include reusable attribution. Tours pause in hidden pages and respect motion preferences.
signature: Map(markers: (Marker | string | Record<string, any>)[], areas?: Area[] | {route?: boolean, tour?: boolean}, center?: string | number[], zoom?: number)

examples.name: Trip plan
examples.code: root = Map([Marker("Belém Tower", [38.6916, -9.216], "daytrip", "16th-century fort on the Tagus. Go early.", "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Lisbon_Torre_de_Bel%C3%A9m_BW_2018-10-03_16-33-21.jpg/960px-Lisbon_Torre_de_Bel%C3%A9m_BW_2018-10-03_16-33-21.jpg", "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bel%C3%A9m_Tower"), Marker("Guesthouse", [38.7118, -9.1300], "stay", "Two nights in Alfama."), Marker("Tram 28 stop", [38.7107, -9.1336], "general", "Ride it uphill, not at noon.", "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Tram_28_Lisbon_Portuguese.jpg/960px-Tram_28_Lisbon_Portuguese.jpg"), Marker("Rua Augusta at noon", [38.7101, -9.1366], "avoid", "Packed with tour groups.")], [Area("Alfama", [[38.7148, -9.1345], [38.7152, -9.1262], [38.7098, -9.1250], [38.7090, -9.1322]], "stay", "Old quarter: steep lanes, good rooms.")])

examples.name: Places by name
examples.code: root = Map([Marker("Lisbon", "Lisbon, Portugal"), Marker("Sintra", "Sintra, Portugal", "daytrip", "Pena Palace and the Moorish Castle."), Marker("Cascais", "Cascais, Portugal", "daytrip", "Beach town at the end of the train line.")])

examples.name: Fixed view
examples.code: root = Map([Marker("Time Out Market", [38.7069, -9.1459], "general", "Food hall by Cais do Sodré.")], null, [38.7069, -9.1459], 16)

examples.name: Days and routes
examples.code: root = Map([{name:"Belém Tower",lat:38.6916,lng:-9.216,day:1,wiki:"Belém Tower",note:"Go early."},{name:"Jerónimos Monastery",lat:38.6979,lng:-9.2067},{name:"Pena Palace",lat:38.7876,lng:-9.3906,day:2,wiki:"Pena Palace"},{name:"Moorish Castle",lat:38.7924,lng:-9.3894}], {route:true,tour:true})

name: Marker
description: One numbered place of Map. at is [lat, lng] or a place name. kind "general" (default, indigo), "stay" (green), "daytrip" (amber), or "avoid" (red). description, image, and link fill its click popup. day groups a trip's stops; later stops inherit it. wiki names an English Wikipedia article whose credited lead photo is looked up only when this place opens.
signature: Marker(title: string, at: string | number[], kind?: "general" | "stay" | "daytrip" | "avoid", description?: string, image?: string, link?: string, day?: string | number, wiki?: string)

name: Area
description: A shaded region of Map: points are three or more [lat, lng] corners in order. kind "general" (default, indigo), "stay" (green), "daytrip" (amber), or "avoid" (red). description shows in its popup.
signature: Area(title: string, points: number[][], kind?: "general" | "stay" | "daytrip" | "avoid", description?: string)

name: Gallery
description: A grid of pictures; clicking one opens it full size, with previous and next. Each item is an image URL or a Photo with a caption. columns is 1 to 6; by default one picture fills the width, two or four sit in pairs, and more go in threes.
signature: Gallery(items: (string | Photo)[], columns?: number)

examples.name: Captioned photos

name: Photo
description: One picture of Gallery: src is an http(s) or data: image URL, caption a short line under it, alt describes it for screen readers (default: the caption).

name: Shader
description: Shadertoy-style WebGL2 shader: code defines void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord). Uniforms include iResolution, iTime, iTimeDelta, iFrame, iMouse, iCamera, iNoise. Named inputs become float uniforms; booleans are 0/1. Up to four buffers run before the image, with ping-pong feedback as iChannel0-3; textures are iTexture0-3. Inputs update uniforms without recompilation. blend is light (black transparent), alpha, or opaque; bloom preserves HDR light. Optional orbit camera, spin, and live height. Rendering pauses off screen and respects reduced motion. No network from shaders; textures load through Pages.
signature: Shader(code: string, height?: number, inputs?: Record<string, number | boolean>, buffers?: string[], textures?: string[], animate?: boolean, blend?: "light" | "alpha" | "opaque", bloom?: number, orbit?: boolean, spin?: number, camera?: {yaw?: number, pitch?: number, zoom?: number})

name: Tests
description: Test results from existing case lists, vitest/Jest JSON, or JUnit XML. Failures sort first, with source locations, messages, and captured output behind disclosures. Search by name, suite, or file. Skips, pending tests, and expected failures stay distinct from passing tests. Load a report with Query("file").
signature: Tests(results: any[] | string | Record<string, any>, title?: string)

examples.name: Cases

name: Threads
description: Threads with their status, branch, and last update. status is active, idle, error, pending, starting, or stopping. waiting true marks a thread that needs an answer; current marks this one. Use Query("threads") for this project.
signature: Threads(threads: {title: string, status?: string, updatedAt?: string | number, branch?: string, waiting?: boolean, current?: boolean}[], title?: string)

examples.name: From the project
examples.code:
data = Query("threads", {limit: 10}, {threads: []})
root = Threads(data.threads)

name: Environments
description: Environments (checkouts and worktrees) with branch, base, and status. status is ready, creating, provisioning, or error. current marks this thread's. Use Query("environments") for this project.
signature: Environments(environments: {name: string, branch?: string, base?: string, status?: string, worktree?: boolean, path?: string, updatedAt?: string | number, current?: boolean}[], title?: string)

examples.name: From the project

data = Query("environments", {}, {environments: []})
root = Environments(data.environments)

name: Board
description: Kanban columns of cards. Each card has a title and a status; cards with the same status share a column. Common statuses ("todo", "in progress", "in review", "blocked", "done") sort in workflow order, others follow as first seen. columns names the columns to show, in order, empty ones too. due is yyyy-mm-dd and shows red once past, unless the card is done. Give name to let the reader move cards (drag, or the ⋯ menu on each card) and send the moves to the thread as "- Card: From → To" lines. Without name it is read-only.
signature: Board(cards: {title: string, status?: string, owner?: string, tags?: string[], due?: string, detail?: string}[], columns?: string[], name?: string)

examples.code: root = Board([{title: "Pricing page copy", status: "todo", owner: "Ana", tags: ["web"]}, {title: "Billing webhooks", status: "in progress", owner: "Raj", due: "2026-10-12"}, {title: "Invoice PDF", status: "in review", owner: "Ana"}, {title: "Tax rules", status: "blocked", detail: "Waiting on legal"}, {title: "Stripe keys", status: "done", owner: "Raj"}])

name: Decision
description: Options for one decision, each with pros, cons, and a note. recommend is the name of the option you recommend; it is marked. Give name to let the reader choose: each option gets a Choose button that sends "<question>: <option>" to the thread, then locks. Without name it is read-only.
signature: Decision(question: string, options: {name: string, pros?: string[], cons?: string[], note?: string}[], recommend?: string, name?: string)

examples.code: root = Decision("Which queue?", [{name: "BullMQ", pros: ["Mature", "Redis we already run"], cons: ["Another Redis load"]}, {name: "SQS", pros: ["No servers"], cons: ["AWS lock-in", "Slower local dev"]}, {name: "Postgres queue", note: "pg-boss on the main DB", pros: ["No new service"], cons: ["Load on the main DB"]}], "BullMQ")

name: Estimate
description: Three-point estimates: per task the best case (low), the likely case, and the worst case (high), with a total. likely defaults to the midpoint. The total also shows P50, P80, and P90 from a PERT model (tasks taken as independent). unit is a short word like "d" (default), "h", "w", or "pts".
signature: Estimate(tasks: {task: string, low: number, likely?: number, high: number}[], unit?: string)

examples.code: root = Estimate([{task: "API", low: 2, likely: 3, high: 6}, {task: "UI", low: 3, likely: 4, high: 8}, {task: "Migration", low: 1, high: 4}, {task: "QA", low: 1, likely: 2, high: 3}])

name: Plan
description: Ordered steps with an owner and a status each. status "todo" (default), "doing", "done", "blocked", or "skipped". due is yyyy-mm-dd or short text like "Fri". A line on top counts done and blocked steps.
signature: Plan(steps: {step: string, status?: "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "blocked" | "skipped", owner?: string, due?: string, detail?: string}[])

name: Roadmap
description: Items on a time axis, grouped by lane. Dates are yyyy-mm-dd; end is the last day. An item with no end, or with milestone true, is a milestone on its start day. status "done", "active", "planned", "at-risk", or "blocked"; without one, an item is active when today is inside it, else planned. The axis reads in days, weeks, or months by span. today defaults to the reader's date.
signature: Roadmap(items: {title: string, start: string, end?: string, lane?: string, status?: "done" | "active" | "planned" | "at-risk" | "blocked", milestone?: boolean}[], today?: string)

name: Acceptance
description: Acceptance checks as a list, a condition matrix, an owner/reviewer result, or CSV text. Existing {criterion,status,evidence,note} rows work. Matrices use {name, cells:{condition:result}} and optional columns. A missing result is not tested; done or owner-reported work is only claimed, not independently verified. Click a condition for its evidence, method, reviewer, run, and time. Required gaps and user actions stay visible.

name: Compare
description: Compare(options, rows, best?) keeps the scored options table. Compare(images, title?, mode?) compares screenshots: images is [{src,label?,meta?,note?}], reference first. mode is side, wipe, blink, or difference. Blink respects motion preferences and can be paused. Inspect changed pixels and regions, adjust tolerance, and zoom in the shared viewer. Different capture conditions and image sizes are disclosed; this is pixel evidence, not design approval.

name: Provenance
description: Two evidence chains. Provenance(claim, steps, value?) keeps the existing source-to-number chain. Provenance(stages, expected?, title?) checks which revision or build reached a device or server. Each stage has {name,status,facts?,evidence?,detail?}; expected holds requested branch/sha/build facts. Missing receipts never pass. Expand a stage for full, copyable facts and evidence; identity changes are flagged.
signature: Provenance(claim: string | any[], steps?: {step: string, value?: string, source?: string, url?: string, detail?: string}[] | Record<string, any>, value?: string)

name: Transcript
description: Speaker-labelled call notes keep the existing [{speaker,text,time?,highlight?}] view. Transcript(tracks, title?, audio?) compares recognizer outputs: the first track is the reference. Each track has {name,words} or {name,text}; Whisper, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, SRT, and WebVTT work. Shows aligned words, word error rate, speaker errors, a zoomable timeline, and error navigation. audio is an optional scoped file or embedded data URL; no transcription service is called.
signature: Transcript(lines: any[] | Record<string, any> | string, title?: string, audio?: string)
